chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Aban ibn Uthman, from the one who informed him, who said:

I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) about a man who has a debt upon him, and in his hand is wealth to pay off his debt, and the wealth belongs to someone else. Is there Zakat upon it? He (peace be upon him) said: When he borrows and a year passes over it, so the Zakat is upon him, if there is an excess in it.
ai.seo_question: Is Zakat due on money held to pay off a debt?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the specific mechanism of Zakat calculation for debtors, establishing that the liability for Zakat rests on the debtor rather than the creditor, provided the borrowed funds have completed a full lunar year (Hawl) in the debtor's possession. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that Zakat is assessed on the net wealth remaining after debt settlement, ensuring that the obligation is not levied on funds merely held in trust for repayment.
